title: AWQ vs GPTQ: kernel-level throughput & latency comparison (May 2026)
content:
Summary:
This is a working note capturing the end-to-end microbenchmark and kernel-level profiling comparing AWQ and GPTQ quantized variants across multiple kernels (Cutlass fused matmul, Triton custom attention, and vendor cuBLAS paths) for 7B and 13B autoregressive models. The goal: capture realistic latency and throughput differences on our Dedicated GPU pools and identify dominant bottlenecks (compute vs memory vs kernel launch overhead) so product can pick sensible defaults for auto-routing and model variant fallbacks.

High-level findings (tl;dr):
- AWQ (4/8 mixed schemes) reduces memory footprint ~1.9-2.2x vs FP16; GPTQ (int8 post-train) reduces ~2.6-3.1x.
- Contrary to expectations, GPTQ int8 often yields better raw throughput on Cutlass matmul kernels for 1K+ token windows, but AWQ's smaller dynamic range and lower PPL regressions give better end-user quality in many prompts.
- Attention kernels are the main bottleneck for chat-like workloads (seq_len <= 512, many short requests). Triton attention kernels show lower latency for AWQ quantized KV-cache hot paths due to fewer memory copies.
- Kernel launch overhead and CPU-side scheduling dominate latency at small batch sizes; batching heuristics in runtime can reclaim much of the throughput loss.

Experiment setup (concise):
- Hardware: G5-16x (NVIDIA H100 cored) and A5000-like dev machines for debugging. Primary results on H100 rack.
- OS/Drivers: Ubuntu 22.04, CUDA 12.2, cuBLAS 12.2, Triton commit 2026-04-30.
- Models: rwi-7b-v1 (causal LM), rwi-13b-v1 (causal LM). We used identical tokenizer and opt configs.
- Quant pipelines:
  - AWQ: per-channel weight + 4-bit accumulation where applicable (AWQ-lite presets from applied-ml branch).
  - GPTQ: per-tensor int8 with fine-tuning of weight groups (GPTQ-v2 script).
  - Baselines: FP16, FP8-e4m3 where supported.
- Kernels evaluated: Cutlass GEMM fused matmul (default runtime), Triton custom fused attention (our optimized kernel), cuBLAS matmul path (fallback).
- Workloads: 1) long-generation (1k token autoreg, batch1), 2) chat short-turns (seq=64/128, many requests), 3) embeddings-like single-token throughput.
- Measurement: median and p95 latency over 300 runs after warm-up; throughput measured as tokens/sec. Also measured GPU SM utilization, memory BW via nvprof, and kernel-level durations from CUDA profiling.

Raw micro-results (examples, medians):
- rwi-7b-v1 (H100, batch1, 1024 tokens):
  - FP16 Cutlass: throughput 18.2 ktoks/s, median latency 55.0s (full generation), mem 22GB
  - GPTQ int8 Cutlass: throughput 29.4 ktoks/s (+61%), median latency 34.1s, mem 7.1GB
  - AWQ 4-bit Cutlass: throughput 24.8 ktoks/s (+36%), median latency 40.2s, mem 9.8GB
  - AWQ (Triton attention + Cutlass matmul): throughput 26.1 ktoks/s, latency 38.2s (less mem copies)

- rwi-13b-v1 (H100, batch1, 1024 tokens):
  - FP16 Cutlass: 9.6 ktoks/s, median 104.3s, mem 38GB
  - GPTQ int8 Cutlass: 15.0 ktoks/s, median 66.8s, mem 12.6GB
  - AWQ 4-bit Cutlass: 12.9 ktoks/s, median 78.1s, mem 18.4GB

Short-turn chat (seq=64, many requests, target latency under 200ms):
- FP16 Triton (fused attention): median per-turn 120ms, p95 210ms
- GPTQ int8 Triton: median 105ms, p95 230ms (slightly worse tail due to occasional dequant path spikes)
- AWQ Triton: median 98ms, p95 180ms (best tail behavior in this scenario)
- Observed that AWQ wins on small seq/p95 because it requires fewer memory staging operations for KV cache update in our Triton implementation.

Perceptual/quality measurements (small eval sets):
- Single-pass PPL on WikiText subset (lower is better):
  - FP16: PPL 13.6 (baseline)
  - GPTQ int8: PPL 15.3 (+12.5%)
  - AWQ 4-bit: PPL 14.8 (+8.8%)
- Downstream slot-filling F1 (small intent dataset): AWQ ~0.9% higher than GPTQ on average, consistent across runs.
- Qualitative: GPTQ introduces occasional tokenization-related hallucinations in longer contexts (rare but reproducible with prompting pattern X).

Kernel-level breakdown (selected):
- For GPTQ int8 on Cutlass path: main matmul kernel occupies ~70% of time during long-gen; matmul kernels are highly SM-bound and achieve >85% occupancy. Memory bandwidth usage ~65% of device peak.
- For AWQ on Triton attention path: attention kernels (fused softmax + causal masking + KV gather) are ~48% of time, matmuls 30%, memory copies 12%, kernel launch overhead ~7%.
- We observed that int8 GEMM kernels are often heavier compute but smaller memory working sets so they convert memory-bound workloads to compute-bound — helpful for throughput when matmul is fused well.

Profiling artifacts and surprises:
- Kernel fragmentation: AWQ's dequant path introduced extra lightweight kernels for scale/zero-point ops which increased launch count and harmed p95 at tiny batches. We mitigated this by fusing dequant scales into the matmul kernel in a Triton prototype (WIP branch).
- cuBLAS fallback for some attention variants produced worse tail latency due to additional device-host syncs in our runtime; avoid for chat workloads.
- FP8 results were unstable across driver versions; e4m3 performed close to FP16 in quality but required tuned kernels. Not recommended as default.

Operational implications for Redwood products:
- Hosted API default: recommend GPTQ-int8 variants for high-throughput batch workloads (embedding generation, long-gen jobs) because of superior tokens/sec and lower memory footprint, but gate with quality monitors.
- Chat/interactive: prefer AWQ variants on Triton fused-attention path to minimize p95 and tail regressions; route small-reqs to AWQ-enabled nodes when latency SLOs matter.
- Runtime should expose per-route quantization policy and a lightweight quality-check eval (small prompt set) to auto-fallback to FP16 if quality regressions exceed threshold.

Open action items (short):
- [x] Land Triton fused dequant->matmul prototype (PR 874) — basic perf improvement validated.
- [ ] Add automated small-prompt quality eval into rollout pipeline (JIRA-RT-1123).
- [ ] Run larger-scale A/B on customer traffic for 7b GPTQ vs AWQ (criteria: p95 latency, error rate, user-visible regressions).
- [ ] Investigate FP8 kernel stability across minor CUDA driver bumps; create matrix tests.
- [ ] Improve runtime telemetry to expose kernel launch counts per request (useful for predicting tail).

Notes to self / developer scribbles:
- Try grouping matmul + dequant scale into a single Triton kernel for 4-bit AWQ — should cut launch overhead ~20-30% on tiny batches.
- Check whether mixed-precision accumulation path could be replaced with 16-bit bias accumulation in AWQ for better numerical stability.
- Re-run rwi-13b long-gen with beam=1 vs beam=4 to see decoding pattern effects.

References and context links: see linked_artifacts above. Also: slack #serving-runtime thread 'awq-gptq-may' (2026-05-10) has interactive traces.

Unresolved questions / risk register (short):
- Some customers on older driver stacks (CUDA 11.x) will see different perf characteristics — need compatibility matrix.
- Will GPTQ int8 generalize to larger models (70B+) without unacceptable PPL hits? Early signs: more aggressive group sizes needed.
- Quantization reproducibility: stochastic elements in GPTQ pipeline cause run-to-run variance; need to check seed management in scripts.

Appendix: brief measurement methodology (repro):
1) Start clean node, kill background daemons, bind runtime to GPU.
2) Load model variant via runtime config with pinned kernel path (cutlass/triton/cublas).
3) Warm-up 50 iterations; then run 300 iterations for med/p95 collection.
4) Collect nvprof traces and runtime telemetry; summarize with script bench/parse-trace.py.

If you want a runnable snapshot, I exported the raw trace tarballs to gcs://redwood-bench/awq-gptq-may2026/ (internal).

Feedback requested:
- Product: are we comfortable exposing both quant variants in Hosted API or should we default one and make the other opt-in?
- Applied ML: validation needed on a larger, more diverse eval suite before any default change.

-- Ruth
